activity.title: 🎓 This was my first summer running Early Career programs at Abridge , and stepping back into intern programming after a few years, I’m reminded of why I loooove this work. In my role I get a front-row seat to watch talented people find their footing and make an impact at a company that's moving fast in AI and healthcare. And witnessing this year’s class doing just that was so rewarding. They worked on projects that are already shaping how care gets delivered: Enhancing our clinical decision support product, building a new demo of Abridge for Nurses, studying how conversations about exercise, sleep, and stress actually show up in primary care visits, and strengthening the safety systems that catch clinical errors before they ever reach a doctor. We held a fireside chat with our CTO San Oo and VP of Product Janie Lee yesterday, and something San said struck me. When asked about the amount of responsibility given to interns at Abridge, he said "You take any amount of responsibility that you want to take, and that's the limit. No one is limiting you, no one is boxing you in, no one's telling you what you can or cannot do. Literally, you are deciding what you can and cannot do." This quote embodies how we think about our early career roles. The projects our interns took on this summer are the kind of ownership people can spend years earning, and they earned it in weeks. I'm grateful to have leaders and managers like San and Janie who genuinely believe in investing in early talent and providing opportunities for exposure and growth. Of course, a summer isn't just what you build, it's who you build it with. Our SF and NY interns had some fun along the way with other employees, like boba and board game nights (with our CEO Shiv (Shivdev) Rao swinging by for a few rounds of Uno), escape room outings, a Broadway show and SF Bay Cruise. Feels fitting with one of our company values, taste good things: you have to taste good things to have good taste. Abridge is committed to hiring interns and early career talent - not as a nice-to-have, but as a real part of how we build this company. If that interests you, keep an eye on our careers page. We have an open Software early career role (below) and will post our upcoming internship positions soon. https://lnkd.in/gFkN2bWm To our Summer 2026 interns - thank you for your energy, your hard work, your contributions to Abridge, and for making this the best part of my year. Happy National Intern Day! Aadyant Maity Aj Sapra Cindy Su Daniel P. Jeong David Fox Emily Byun Hasan Siddiqui Hayoung Jung Jonathan Kong Jonathan Liu Jonathan Ouwerx Nicole Chiou Pranav Manjunath Sanjit Dandapanthula Shuvom Sadhuka Tanya Bhatia

We’re live! Nook is a campus-focused app built to help University of Washington students quickly and efficiently find the best study spots. On a campus where library crowding and unpredictable noise can make studying stressful, Nook provides real-time insights into study environments across campus, making it easier to focus and stay productive. With Nook, you can: - View crowd and noise levels of study spots in real time - Bookmark and rate your favorite “nooks” for easy return - Use built-in study timers to stay focused and track productivity - Join the community feature to see where friends are studying and stay motivated together If you're a Husky, download Nook now!
